subject.title: Google Chat: agent-to-agent (bot↔bot) conversation doesn't work — a Chat app doesn't receive messages from another Chat app (same setup works on Discord)

question: Should OpenClaw handle this as a Google Chat documentation limitation only, or sponsor an opt-in channel-independent bridge for agent-to-agent conversations?
rationale: Current code already has explicit A2A session tooling, but automatically translating channel output or logical mentions into cross-agent messages would define new product behavior across security, routing, and loop-prevention boundaries.

options.title: Document now, design bridge separately
options.body: Add the Google Chat caveat and point users at explicit `sessions_send` A2A tooling while leaving any automatic bridge for a separate maintainer-approved design.

options.title: Sponsor an opt-in bridge
options.body: Define a cross-channel bridge contract that reuses existing A2A policy and validates live Google Chat behavior before implementation.

options.title: Close as platform limitation
options.body: Treat Google Chat app-to-app delivery as outside OpenClaw scope and avoid adding bridge semantics.

recommendation.title: Document now, design bridge separately
recommendation.body: Add the Google Chat caveat and point users at explicit `sessions_send` A2A tooling while leaving any automatic bridge for a separate maintainer-approved design.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses generic bot-loop protection and multi-agent/session tooling, where this owner has the strongest current history signal.
